justification: A uses bold sans-serif numbered headings that stand out clearly from the serif body text, so the hierarchy is easy to scan (A1, A2). B's light serif headings are weak, and the red rules above every section add clutter. B's table is slightly more spacious, but the stat row and callout are about equal in both. A also has a running header and footer with page count, while B has a heavy red band at the top of page 2. B's justified text has some awkward hyphenation of 'recommended'. A has a similar hyphenation of 'mobilisation'.

A keeps the allocation table whole on A2 and pairs the charts with the river section on A3. B splits the table across B2 and B3, repeating its header and leaving Farming and Towns separated from Industry, reserve and Total. B's full-bleed bands and the serif body feel heavier, though its running header and footer are nicer. A's last page is mostly empty, but this is a minor flaw next to the split table.

A packs the highlights, portfolio table and bar chart together on A2, so the chart sits beside the data it illustrates. Its section rules and indented body text give a clean, even rhythm, and the pages are well filled. B strands the bar chart on B3 away from its table, leaves a large gap on B2, and leaves B5 nearly empty. B's heavy header and footer bands add chrome, though its numbered headings and teal-and-navy colour are tidy. B's cover is centred and balanced, while A's low-left cover is more distinctive.

B packs content more densely across 3 pages, so there are no mostly empty pages. A leaves page 1 more than half blank and page 4 almost entirely empty apart from the table. B also keeps the mission and image together on its cover page and adds a running header band for continuity. A splits the Arabic caption text away from its image and gives the Finance section no table on its own page. B's Arabic typeface is larger and easier to read, though B does push one Arabic paragraph onto the next page, which separates it from its section.

A keeps the portfolio table and its chart together on A2, and the content fills pages more evenly. Its bold geometric headings are clear, and its minimal cover is elegant. B's colour bands on the cover and in the headers and footers look polished, but they take up space. B splits the portfolio chart from its table (B1/B2), and its light headings are weaker. B also leaves large empty areas at the bottoms of B2, B3 and B4, so the page rhythm is uneven. A's last page is also somewhat empty, but less so.

B keeps the allocation table whole on B2, while A splits it across A2 and A3 and repeats the header. B's sans type is cleaner and its Arabic pairs better with the Latin text. A's full-bleed bands and larger serif text read well, but A3 and A4 leave large gaps and the table split breaks the flow. B4 is mostly empty, but B2 and B3 are denser and more cohesive.

A opens with a full-bleed illustrated cover and a brown band carrying a centred title (A1). Its bold sans headings are numbered and stand out clearly against the serif body text (A2). Its inner pages are dense, but they keep a steady rhythm of text, image, stats and table. A's paragraph split across pages 2 and 3 is a flaw. B starts with a brown header block and a wrapped title, which is clumsier (B1). B also puts the cover and first section on one page, and its headings are lighter and weaker. B's page 3 leaves a large empty area under the table (B3). B's per-page header with logo and its more complete page footer are small positives. B's Arabic title wraps awkwardly.

B pairs a serif with its Arabic and uses thin gold rules, so it reads as a calm, editorial report. Its text flows across pages with even spacing, and the cover is a single cohesive image with the title set low (B1). A's heavy teal banners are blunt. Its page 4 is mostly empty and its page 3 has a large gap at the bottom (A3, A4). A's cover splits into an image and a flat block (A1). Its table header wraps awkwardly (A2). B's table header also wraps, but it is more refined (B2).

A keeps the allocation table whole on A2, while B splits it across B2 and B3 and repeats the header. A's refined serif text and thin gold rules give a calm hierarchy, and its cover puts the title over the illustration. B's heavy teal bands are blunt, and its larger text is less refined. B also separates the photo from its section on B3/B4, leaving large gaps on B3. A's page 3 has some empty space, but it is more coherent.

A opens with a strong navy title band over the highlights, so the first page carries content and its running header and footer bands tie the pages together. It fits the document in 4 pages with a consistent rhythm, though the sparse last page and the small, cramped cash cover chart (A3) are weaker. B spends a whole page on a mostly empty navy cover (B1), and its pages sit under a thin rule with a quiet footer, which is elegant but less structured. B's serif typography and its larger, clearer charts (B3, B4) are real strengths, but B's sparse final page (B5) and extra page count make it less efficient overall.

B has a navy cover band, section divider pages with a side index, and running header and footer bands, which give clear navigation and a consistent system (B1, B2, B5). Its income statement and financial position share one page and read as one set (B6). A splits the income statement across two pages, repeating the header and leaving page 5 mostly empty (A4, A5). A's overlay box covers the image (A6), while B places the callout cleanly beside it (B7). A's pages carry large empty areas and the hierarchy is thinner, though its clean headings and the full-bleed image are good.

B packs content into three pages with the hero image on the cover and a running header and footer. Its stat figures are brown and tie in with the cover band. The finance table sits directly under its intro text. A leaves A1 more than half empty and puts the table alone on A4, which is almost entirely blank. In A, the Arabic overflow paragraph below the image on A3 is separated from its English text, and the overlay card covers the image. B has a similar split, with the Arabic paragraph stranded on B3, which is a minor flaw. A's cover title wraps awkwardly.

A is a tighter five-page document with consistent serif headings, a clean gold rule and a small header, and the text and tables fill the pages sensibly. B adds divider pages that waste space; its sidebar title wraps awkwardly across lines (B2), and its heavy header and footer bands make the content pages feel more mechanical. B's section dividers are bold and give clear navigation, but the extra pages and large empty areas on B3, B4 and B7 weaken the rhythm. Tables and charts are nearly identical in both.

A uses strong teal section bands, a full-bleed cover with a colored title block, and a compact 4-page flow. The table header is clear and the image sits mid-page with its caption. B has weaker thin-rule headings and a cover with a large empty lower area. Page 3 of B is half empty and the image is pushed to the next page. Page 5 holds one orphaned paragraph on an otherwise blank page, which breaks the rhythm. B's serif body is elegant but the layout is more fragmented.

A's English serif is larger and darker, and it pairs with a Noto Naskh Arabic of matching size, so the two scripts feel balanced (A1, A2). In B the Arabic is a heavier, larger sans that overpowers the small light English serif, so the bilingual text looks mismatched (B1, B2). B's cover title splits cleanly across two lines, but the stray bar after the Arabic looks odd. A's title wraps awkwardly, with the Arabic broken across lines. B's callout card sits over the image, which is a nice layered touch, but it hides most of the buildings. A's callout block sits beside the image and reads more cleanly (A2). The tables are about equal (A3, B3).

A opens with a strong full-bleed illustrated cover and a brown band, then packs content into dense, evenly filled pages. Headings are clear, the stat row is bold, and the finance table sits on the same page as its intro. B's page 1 is mostly empty after the brief mission text, and page 4 holds only a table with a large blank area. B's pull quote also overlaps the building image awkwardly, and the Arabic text is small. A has a minor flaw: the Programmes paragraph breaks across pages.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body, numbers the sections, and gives clear heading weight (A2, A4). B's headings are thin and light, so they barely stand out from the body, and its teal rules add clutter (B2, B3). A's charts are taller and easier to read, with a fuller axis, while B's are squat with only a few ticks (B2, B3). B's cover band is strong and merges the cover with the first content page, but A's separate cover is calmer. A's justified text has some hyphenation gaps, but this is minor.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so the section headings stand out clearly (A1, A2). B uses light serif headings that barely differ from the body text, so hierarchy is weaker (B1, B2). A's headings sit flush left while the body is indented, which looks a little odd. B's margins are cleaner and its red rules and top bar on page 2 look polished. B's title also fits on one line. Overall A has the stronger scanning structure.

B uses strong teal section bands, a colored cover panel and a consistent running header, and fills its pages evenly, ending in four pages. A leaves pages 3 and 5 mostly empty, and page 5 holds only one orphaned paragraph. A's table is whole on one page with a good layout, but B splits its table across pages 2 and 3 with a repeated header. B's larger text is also easier to read.

A uses a clean sans-serif with a running header band on page 2 and a footer that reads 'Northline Transit, Page 2 of 2'. Its stat figures are bold and clear against the purple theme. B's serif is elegant, but its text is smaller and looser. Its page 2 has a stray red rule at the top and no header band, so it feels less finished. The tables are about equal. Both leave a lot of empty space at the bottom of each page.

A keeps the allocation table whole on A2, and the charts sit with the section that follows. B splits the table across B2 and B3, repeating its header, which breaks the reading of the data. B's full-width teal bands give strong section markers, but they eat vertical space and leave large empty areas on B3. A's flow is more continuous and its sections read more cleanly, though the text at the top of A4 is detached from its heading.

A gives each section its own page, with a consistent running header, a gold rule, and a strong navy cover band (A1). Its finance tables stay whole on one page with clear navy headers (A4). Stat blocks and charts sit with the operations text (A3). B splits the income statement across pages and repeats its header (B4, B5). B also leaves the chair's page mostly empty (B2) and separates the operations stats from their text (B3, B4). B's apprenticeship callout covers part of the image (B6).

A fits the cover, mission text and hero image on page 1, and keeps a running header band and a consistent footer. Section rules and the stat row on A2 hold together well, and the finance table sits with its intro on A3. B leaves most of its cover empty (B1) and its Finance heading is stranded from its table, which lands alone on B4 (B3, B4). B's stat row and image are fine, but its inconsistent left edges and large dead areas weaken the flow.

B keeps its tables whole on one page (B4), while A splits the income statement across pages and repeats the header (A4, A5), leaving A5 half empty. B has a consistent running header and gold rule, steady page structure, and larger Arabic text that reads better beside the English. A's chair page is sparse with an empty lower half (A2), and its cover has a white bottom third with the title floating (A1). B's cover is cohesive with the title set over the artwork (B1). A's full-bleed image on A3 is strong, but overall B is more polished and consistent.

A keeps the cover band, mission text and image together on page 1. Its year-in-brief and programmes sections share page 2, and the finance table sits with its intro on page 3. B leaves page 1 mostly empty and strands the finance table alone on page 4, with a large blank gap beneath it. B's Arabic text is also smaller than the English beside it, and its section headings are weaker. A's Arabic is larger and matches the English better, and its headings are clearer.

A's serif body and bold serif title look more refined and board-paper appropriate. Its larger KPI numerals and looser line spacing read comfortably (A1). B's sans-serif is clean and its running header band on page 2 adds navigation (B2), but its tighter text and heavier title feel more generic. The tables are near-identical (A2, B2). A's thin red rule at the top of page 2 is a nice touch, but B's header band is more functional.

A has bold numbered section headings that stand out clearly (A2), a bright, high-contrast cover with a teal band (A1), and larger body text that reads easily. B's section headings are light and small, and its text is thinner, so the hierarchy is weaker. B's dark cover is moody and refined, with a nice gold rule and running header (B1, B2), but its low contrast is less striking. Both tables are similar, and in both the charts and the continued section sit awkwardly at the top of a page.

A gives each section its own page with a serif and Arabic pairing, a full-bleed atmospheric cover and a pull-quote overlaid on the image. B packs sections together, so Finance starts at the bottom of B3 and its table lands on B4 under a People and safety header. B4 then carries the People and safety text and B5 is mostly empty, which breaks the rhythm. B's heavy header and footer bands add clutter. Tables are nearly identical in both.

B groups each section with its own content: Finance with its tables on B4, People and safety with its image on B5. A splits sections across pages. Its Finance heading is stranded at the foot of A3, away from the tables on A4, and the People and safety text on A4 is separated from its image on A5. A5 is mostly empty with a lone Arabic line, and A2 and A3 have dead space at the bottom. B's serif type is slightly larger and its running footer is quieter, while A's dark header and footer bands are stronger but heavier. B's balance is better because every page is filled more evenly.

A uses teal section bands that give clear hierarchy and a consistent rhythm across four pages with a filled cover. B has small, weak headings and large empty areas on A3-equivalent pages. B5 holds only one orphaned paragraph, and B3 is mostly blank. B's allocation table is complete on one page, which is a plus, whereas A splits its table across pages 2 and 3 and repeats the header. Overall A is more cohesive and polished.

A reads as a more editorial annual statement: a brown title band on a cover page, a full-bleed landscape image, and large stat numerals (A2). Each section stays whole and clean. A's weaknesses are large empty areas on A1 and A4, where the table sits alone on a mostly blank page. B is denser and has a strong cover, but a paragraph splits across pages 2 and 3 ("traditional / dhow construction"), which looks like a flaw. B's repeated mission image is redundant, the pull quote block is heavy, and the cramped layout loses some rhythm (B2, B3).

B keeps each section together: the Arabic school-visits paragraph sits under the image on B2, so it reads as a continuation of the section. A splits that Arabic paragraph onto A3, where it is orphaned above Finance and breaks the flow. B's brown header band on pages 2-3 anchors the page more strongly than A's thin logo header. B's sans type is clean and keeps the Arabic and Latin matched; A's serif pairs less evenly. The tables are about equal, and A's is slightly larger. The large empty space on A3 and B3 is similar.

A packs each section onto one page with a consistent gold rule header, so the sections pace evenly. Its stats, charts and both finance tables sit together on A3 and A4. B splits the income statement across B4 and B5, repeating the header on a near-empty page, and leaves B2 mostly blank. B's Arabic text is also small and light next to the English. B's cover is clean, but A's cover is moodier and has a stronger title block.

A is more cohesive and compact. Its navy header and footer bands and gold rules give a clear structure, and the cover title sits on a navy panel. The income statement and financial position tables sit together on A4, while B splits the income statement across two pages (B4, B5) and leaves B5 mostly empty. A's KPI figures, charts and text flow well on A3, with bar charts in navy and grey. B's serif body text is pleasant, but its pages are less filled, its pull-quote overlaps the apprenticeship image awkwardly (B6), and the large repeated image on B3 wastes space. A's last page (A5) is also sparse.

A pairs an elegant serif with light rules and has a dark full-bleed cover (A1), so the document feels refined and cohesive. Its headings are light serif with teal rules and the tables are clean (A2-A4). B's heavy navy header and footer bands repeat on every page and add clutter, and its numbered sans headings feel more generic (B2-B5). B's cover is centred but plain (B1). Both have a sparse last page.

A gives each section its own page with a consistent header, clear bilingual headings and a serif/sans pairing. Its pages feel complete and calm (A2-A5). B runs sections together: Finance starts at the bottom of B3 with its table on B4, and People and safety is split between B4 and B5, leaving B5 mostly empty and breaking the rhythm. B's header and footer bands are heavy, though they are clear. B's Arabic type is rendered well, but its thin heading weight is weaker than A's.

A has a dark navy cover with a teal accent rule, and a teal band across the top of each page. Its serif headings are elegant and consistent, and it lets each section breathe. Charts are placed close to the sections they illustrate (A3, A4). B is denser. Its bold sans headings are indented relative to the body text, which looks misaligned (B2). The chart is split from its related paragraph, which carries over to the next page (B3). B also leaves the last page awkwardly mixed, with the chart and the appendix sharing it (B4). A's last page is sparse, though, and A5 is mostly empty.

A uses bold numbered section headings in a sans face over a serif body, so the sections are easy to find on A1 and A2. B uses light, thin headings with red rules above each one. These headings are weaker and the rules add clutter (B1, B2). B's full-width header band on page 2 is a nice touch. A's body text is slightly easier to read, though it has some awkward hyphenation. B also hyphenates, as in 're-commended'. The tables and KPI rows are about equal.

B packs content into 4 pages with consistent gold rules, a running header and a larger Arabic size that matches the English. Its charts and photo sit with the text, and the table is clean. A leaves large empty areas on A3 and A5, where one paragraph is stranded on its own page. A's Arabic is small next to the English, and its pages feel uneven. A's cover is strong, but B's full-bleed cover with the title overlaid is more cohesive.

A's cover title wraps awkwardly, but the rest holds together. Its running header band, the callout beside the cityscape, and its page 2 closing paragraph all read cleanly. B's callout box covers most of the buildings and clips the image. Its page 2 text spills onto page 3, leaving an orphaned Arabic paragraph at the top of page 3. B's serif English paired with the Arabic looks refined, and its cover title wraps better. Even so, A's page flow and image/callout handling are more coherent.

B's pages look more polished and consistent. Its Arabic text is larger and better matched to the English, and its serif body face is more elegant (B2, B3). Its cover is a full-bleed image with the title block placed low, which looks more refined than A's split cover with a flat blue block and a dead lower half (A1, B1). B's page 5 overlays the callout on the image, which integrates better than A's separate blue box beside the image (A5, B5). B's tables are clean and similar to A's, but with more comfortable row spacing (A4, B4). A's running headers and footers are more detailed, but its Arabic is smaller and the English column is narrow, giving a cramped feel (A2).

A uses a consistent left margin with light-weight headings, coloured stat figures and a running header band on page 2, giving a cohesive look. B indents the body under hanging bold headings, which leaves a narrow text column. B's title wraps awkwardly onto two lines, and its page 2 has no header band. A's one weakness is the hyphenated 're-commended', but B also hyphenates 'mobil-isation'.

Design A is compact: sections flow on shared pages with consistent gold rules and headings, though A5 is mostly empty and A4 splits People and safety from the tables. Design B adds two divider pages (B2, B5) with a sidebar nav band and large numbered headings, which makes the structure clear but leaves them mostly blank and adds length. B's serif body text on B3 and B4 is warmer, but the pairing with the Arabic type is slightly less cohesive. Overall A is tighter and more even in rhythm. B's section numbering and dividers read as more polished, yet B has more dead space (B3, B4, B7). The call is close.

A pairs a serif body with a refined heading style, and its full-bleed navy cover gives a polished, report-like start (A1). Its tables and charts are larger and clearer, with a fuller y-axis on the charts (A3, A4). Its pages are consistent and have a calm rhythm and a quiet footer (A2-A5). B puts the title in a header band that competes with the content, and its sans-serif text is heavier and tighter. B's repeated header and footer bands add clutter, its charts are squashed with sparse axes, and the pages leave large empty areas (B2-B4). A's final page is also sparse, but overall A reads as the more elegant document.

B uses solid teal section bands, a running header and a tinted cover panel, so headings stand out clearly. Its table has a strong header, and its content flows across four pages with the image placed near its text (B3). A is five pages with large empty areas: A3 is half empty, and A5 carries only one paragraph. A's headings are thin rules with small bold text, and its table header is a black bar. Its image is pushed to the top of a page, away from related text (A4).

A's sans-serif type is clean and consistent across Latin and Arabic, and its solid brown header band reads well on every page (A2, A3). Its text blocks stay compact and each section holds together on its page, with the Arabic carry-over line kept under the image on A2. B's serif Latin sits awkwardly beside the Arabic. B also splits the Programmes text onto page 3, where an orphaned Arabic paragraph opens the page (B3). B's thin header with a logo is fussier. Both layouts leave large empty areas at the bottom of page 3, and the tables are near-identical.

A fits the content on four pages with a dark cover band, consistent gold rules, and larger Arabic that pairs well with the English. The table and charts sit well, and the image comes right after its section text. B runs to five pages. B3 has a large empty lower half, and B5 holds one orphaned paragraph on an otherwise blank page. B's Arabic is smaller and the image is detached from its section, so the flow is less even.

B uses teal header bands for section titles and a running header, giving clear structure (B2, B3, B4). Its image is inset and aligned to the text margins, and its charts sit more neatly in the grid (B3). A has plain headings and no bands. Its section 2 heading lacks emphasis, its section 3 chart row starts a page with little context, and its image is narrower than the text column with an awkward caption (A3). A's section 3 text splits across pages 3 and 4, leaving page 4 mostly empty (A4). B's page 4 is also sparse, though it keeps sections together. The tables are nearly identical (A2, B2).

A has a more refined, editorial look. Its cover sets the title over a dusk landscape with a gold rule. Its interior pages use gold dividers, a branded header and a serif body that feels cohesive (A1, A2). The photo spans the full text width and the charts sit tidily above it (A3). B's cover is decent but plain, and its numbered headings in a heavy sans feel more generic. B's body text is larger and slightly easier to read, and its running header is useful. However, the chart label wraps awkwardly in B3, and its image is narrower than the text column. Both tables are similar.

A opens with a strong navy title band and puts the highlights and KPIs on the same first page, so the document starts with content. B's cover is a mostly empty page with a small centred title. B's serif body and numbered headings are readable, and its charts are larger and clearer (B3, B4). A's line chart is small and its axis is truncated (A3). A is more compact and consistent, but it leaves large empty areas at the bottom of A2, A3 and A4. B has similar gaps on B5.

A splits the allocation table across pages 2 and 3, repeating its header, and leaves a large empty area at the bottom of page 3. B keeps the whole table on page 2 where it is easy to read and compare. A's full-width teal bands give strong section markers, which is a plus. But B's numbered headings are clean, and its flow of text, charts and image is more even. B does leave page 4 half empty, and its charts sit awkwardly at the top of page 3, separated from the section they belong to.

Design B pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, and numbered headings read clearly as sections (B1, B2). Its headings are heavier and the text is easy to scan. Design A uses thin light headings with red rules, which gives a more consistent rhythm and clear section breaks, but its headings are weaker. A also has a hyphenated 'Option B is re-commended' and wide letterspacing in its justified text (A2). Both have large empty areas at the bottom of each page. The tables are nearly identical. Overall B has the stronger hierarchy and readability, but the margin is small.

B packs the content into 4 pages with sensible pagination. Its numbered headings are larger and its Arabic text is bigger and easier to read (B2). The teal cover band and the framed image tie the document together (B1, B3). A spreads the same content over 5 pages and leaves large empty areas. A3 is half empty and A5 holds a single paragraph. A's section headings are small, and its image bleeds awkwardly on A4. A's cover has a stronger plain-white title area, but its lower half is left empty (A1). Overall B is more cohesive and keeps better rhythm.

A uses a serif/Arabic pairing with a clear title lockup that sits comfortably on two lines in the cover band (A1). Its table is airy with a clear net row (A3). The overflow of the school-visits Arabic text onto page 3 is awkward, since the callout overlays the image and the Arabic translation is split off from it. B's cover title wraps awkwardly into three lines, with Arabic broken across lines (B1). B does have a better integrated callout/image split and running header bands (B2, B3), but the sans-serif body is plainer and its table is tighter. The Arabic paragraph under the image in B2 also sits cramped against the caption.

B keeps the allocation table whole on B2, while A splits it across A2 and A3 and repeats the header. B's cover is a full-bleed image with the title set low, which looks more refined than A's split cover. B's thin gold rules and lighter type feel calmer and more editorial. A's heavy teal bands give stronger section hierarchy, but they take up space and leave awkward empty areas on A3 and A4. B's Arabic type is larger and sits better beside the English. B has some loose space on B3 and B4.

A pairs an elegant serif with a clean Arabic face. Its cover title sits on one line per language, and the dark band is more refined. B's cover title wraps awkwardly, splitting the Arabic across lines (B1). A's Arabic text is larger and better matched to the Latin (A2), though B's body text is larger and easier to read. A's overlay callout on the image is slightly cramped, while B's side-by-side layout is cleaner (B2). B's header and footer are more informative, but A is more polished overall. Both tables are similar.

B is more cohesive. It has navy header and footer bands and gold rules, and a navy cover panel that ties into the artwork (B1, B2). Its pages are denser and better filled, so the dashboard KPIs and charts sit with Operations (B3) and both financial tables fit on one page (B4). A leaves large empty areas, splits the income statement across pages and repeats the table header (A4, A5), and leaves pages 2 and 6 half empty. A's cover is clean and its serif body is elegant. Its overlay callout hides the illustration (A6), whereas B's side-by-side callout is clearer (B5). B's final page is mostly empty, though.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so the section headings stand out clearly (A1, A2). B's light, thin headings are weaker, and its justified text opens wide word gaps and an awkward 're-commended' break (B2). B does have a better title band that fits on one line and a running header band on page 2. A's title wraps onto two lines, and A's indented body text is a little uneven against the headings. A's big black KPI numbers are stronger than B's purple ones. Overall A's hierarchy is clearer.

B reads as a more refined report: a serif English face pairs well with the Arabic, and the cover gets a full-bleed image with the title set over it. Each page has a consistent gold rule and logo mark, and the finance page is cleanly separated from Operations. Its tables are airy and legible. A's sans text is fine, but its heavy header and footer bands compete with the content. Page 4 jams the tables against a text section, and page 5 is mostly empty with a cramped callout. B's page 5 overlays the quote on the image more convincingly, though the callout hides part of the buildings.

B packs content into 3 pages with a consistent flow: the hero image sits under the mission, the stats follow, and the pull quote is a clean brown block beside the illustration. A leaves page 1 mostly empty, puts the image alone on page 2 with a large blank top margin, and its pull quote box covers part of the illustration. A's table sits alone on a nearly empty page 4, with the finance intro stranded on page 3. B keeps the finance intro with its table and adds running header bands. B's Arabic title wraps awkwardly, but overall it is more cohesive.

B has a full-bleed dark cover with a left-aligned title, a serif heading style and teal rules that give a more refined, report-like feel (B1, B2). Its tables and charts are cleanly spaced with generous margins (B3, B4). A's bold sans headings with numbering are clearer and its header and footer bands aid navigation, but they feel heavier. A's cover is plain and centred (A1). Both leave page 5 mostly empty. The call is close, and I lean toward B for its polish, but the criteria scores above are inconsistent in sign and should be read with caution.

A fills its cover page with the mission text and the hero image, and the 3-page flow is tight. Its header band, running header and section rules are consistent. B leaves most of the cover page empty (B1). It also splits the Finance heading from its table across pages, and page 4 holds only a small table with the rest blank (B3, B4). B's callout box covers the buildings awkwardly and its left margins are inconsistent. A's one flaw is the Arabic paragraph orphaned at the top of A3, and its page 3 also has a large empty lower half.

A has a centred cover, navy header and footer bands that carry the section name and page number, numbered headings, and a navy chart colour that matches the tables. Its KPI row and tables are clean. Page 5 is mostly empty, which is a weakness. B is compact and tidy, but it has no bands, a left-aligned cover, and unnumbered headings of near-equal weight. Its chart is black and the appendix is demoted to a small heading. B also uses a more consistent page flow, but the overall look is plainer and the body text is offset from the headings.

Design B is more cohesive. Its text block is aligned and uses the page width consistently, and its numbered headings sit flush with the body, so the structure reads clearly (B1, B2). The running header and footer with page count add polish, and the table fits the content width (B2). Design A indents the body against flush-left headings with rules, which leaves a ragged left edge. Its table is slightly narrower than the rules above it. The right margin is also uneven, and the footer is sparse (A1, A2). A's heading rules and title band are decent, but B is tidier overall.

Scores are signed toward A when positive and B when negative. B has a stronger cover with a full illustration, section divider pages with a navigation sidebar, and running header and footer bands that add structure. B's text is larger and its tables are cleaner, with a clear Arabic and English split. B's pull-quote callout beside the image on its final page is also stronger. A is cleaner and more minimal, but its cover is dark and flat, and its pages have more empty space at the bottom. A's smaller body text and weaker bands make it less engaging. B's divider pages are mostly empty, and its heading wraps awkwardly on B2. Overall B is slightly better.

B is more readable: larger body text, fuller tables, and a cover with a clear image band above a solid title block. B also has running headers and footers with section names. A has a more atmospheric cover, but its small text and pale moon are less legible. A's tables and charts are neat but small, and its callout overlay on the page 5 image is elegant but crowds the picture. B's page 5 callout panel is clearer.

A has divider pages with a sidebar contents band that marks each section, and each section starts on its own page with a clear heading and a consistent serif body face. B packs sections together, so Finance starts at the foot of page 3 and its tables land on page 4 under the People and safety header. The People and safety section is also split awkwardly in B, leaving page 5 mostly empty with a stray Arabic line. A has some empty space on its pages, but the structure reads as more deliberate. The tables in both are similar.

A has a 4-page flow with a teal title band on the cover, numbered and larger section headings, and a teal table header. Content is packed efficiently, so the pages stay coherent. B spills to a fifth page that holds a single orphaned paragraph, leaves large empty areas on B3 and B5, and places the image at the top of B4, detached from its section. B's section headings are small and weak. B's black table header is fine but less cohesive than A's.

A adds tabbed section-divider pages (A2, A5) with a highlighted contents sidebar, and dark header and footer bands on the content pages, which give clearer navigation and a stronger structure. Its sans and serif pairing is also more distinct. B is consistent and clean, with a logo header and gold rule. But it has no dividers or bands, and the pages feel plainer (B2-B5). A's divider pages are mostly empty and its body pages have large bottom gaps (A3, A7), though B has similar gaps (B5). The tables and charts are nearly identical in both (A6, B4).

A uses full-width teal section bands on A2, A3 and A4, which give clear hierarchy and structure. Its sans-serif body type is consistent with the Arabic. B's plain numbered headings are weaker, its serif body mixes less cleanly with the Arabic, and its chart label wraps awkwardly on B3. B also splits a section across pages, leaving the replanting paragraph orphaned on B4. A's full-width image on A3 is stronger than B's inset image, although A leaves a large empty area on A4.

A has a full-bleed navy cover band and section dividers with a sidebar contents band (A2, A5). Each section starts cleanly on its own page with a clear heading. Tables stay intact on A6, with the income statement complete. B splits the income statement across pages (B4, B5) and repeats its header. B also crams sections together, and its dark overlay hides the building image (B6). A's header and footer bands give a steadier rhythm.

A keeps each section's English and Arabic paragraphs together, with a clear dark header band and a calm structure. B's paragraph breaks across pages (the 'Programmes' text splits between B2 and B3) and its Arabic continuation sits orphaned below the image on B3, which hurts reading. B's cover is striking, but its body pages feel crowded and its images are cut off. A does leave a stray Arabic paragraph at the top of A3 and a lot of empty space at the bottom of A3.

A keeps each section whole: the mission, year-in-brief and programmes blocks sit cleanly on pages 1-2, and the finance table has its own page (A2, A3). B splits the programmes paragraph across pages, leaving "dhow construction alive in two yards." stranded at the top of B3. It also repeats the cover image on B2. B's full-bleed cover with a brown band is strong (B1), but its interior pages are crowded and break awkwardly. A's tall brown header band and its Arabic/English headings read well. A does leave page 3 half empty, and its Arabic paragraph on A3 is orphaned from the school-visits block.

B packs content into five pages with sections flowing consistently, and the finance tables (B4) stay together on one page. A splits the income statement across pages and repeats the table header (A4-A5). A also leaves large empty areas (A2, A5, A6), and its text column is indented and narrow. B's overlay panel on the apprenticeship image is cleaner (B5) than A's dark box covering the image (A6). B has a branded header and a navy cover band that looks more polished (B1). A has a stronger bold sans title on its cover (A1).

A uses a consistent serif system with a one-line title and red rules over light headings, and its text aligns with the rules and the table on both pages. B has a title wrapping to two lines and heavy sans headings hung in the left margin with indented body text, so the layout is lopsided and the rules run past the text edge. The tables and stat blocks are similar in both. A also has a red top band on page 2 and a more refined page footer.

A has a strong navy title band and clean tables, but its pages end with large empty areas (A2 about 35% blank, A3 and A4 mostly empty). The chart on A2 is separated from the table it illustrates on A1. The appendix alone on A4 is nearly empty. B has a quiet cover, then fuller pages. Its table, chart and text flow is steadier, and its serif body with bold sans headings reads well (B2, B3, B4). B's bands are weaker, since it has only rules and no header or footer bars, but its page rhythm is much more even.

Design B is more compact and consistent. Every page has the same gold rule, logo mark and quiet footer, and the same heading position, so the rhythm is steady (B2-B5). Its serif headings and body text, with wider measures, read more calmly. The tables are clean (B4). The cover places the title over the image in an elegant way (B1). Design A has full-page divider pages that add bulk and leave large empty areas. A's cover has a heavy blue block with a lot of dead space. A's heavy header and footer bars crowd the pages, and its body columns are narrow (A3, A4). A's tables are good, though (A6). A's callout image is well composed (A7), but B's overlay callout partly covers the buildings (B5).

A gives each section a clear start: a brown title band on the cover and a teal rule over each heading. Its page 2 keeps the programmes text together with the callout, and the finance page stays whole, although page 3 is mostly empty. B has a striking full-bleed cover (B1), but the Programmes paragraph splits across pages 2 and 3 (B2, B3), which breaks the flow. B also crowds sections into the pages, and its image appears twice, once on the cover and again as a small inset on B2. A's cover image is wide and anchors the page (A1).

B's tinted cover band, top rule and consistent margins make it feel more finished, and its serif body is comfortable to read. However, A is the more compact and balanced design. Its bold sans headings give a clearer hierarchy, and its tables and charts sit next to the text they support on pp. A2-A4. B's chart is separated from its table and its pages end in large empty areas (B2, B5). A also has flaws: headings sit left of the indented body text, so the alignment is odd, and the cover is plain white. Overall A is slightly better on structure and B on polish; I lean A.

A pairs a refined serif with light headings and red rules that separate sections clearly (A1, A2). Its spacing is more generous and the rhythm more even. B's bold sans headings with numbers are clear but heavier, and its justified text shows wide gaps and awkward breaks such as 'mo-bilisation' (B2). B's running header and footer are useful, but the pages feel more crowded.

B keeps each section's text together: the Programmes paragraph is complete on B2, and the Finance section stays whole on B3. A splits the Programmes paragraph across A2 and A3 ('keeping traditional / dhow construction alive'), which hurts reading. A's cover is a strong full-bleed image, but B's cover is a solid brown band with a title that wraps awkwardly across three lines. A's bold section headings are clearer than B's light ones. B's running header band and consistent section rules give an even rhythm, though B3 is mostly empty below the table.

A keeps one consistent left margin, with numbered headings, a running header and a footer with the page count. The title fits on one line in the purple band (A1). B has an odd layout: headings hang in the left margin while the body is indented, and the rules above each heading add clutter. B's title wraps awkwardly, and its band is taller with misaligned content (B1, B2). A's tables and callouts sit cleanly on the text column (A2).

A pairs an elegant serif with refined gold rules and a moody cover with the title overlaid on the artwork (A1). Its text pages are airy, and the table is clean (A2). B's heavy teal section bands and running headers feel generic and dense (B2, B3). B's cover splits the image from a flat teal block, and its last page is mostly empty (B4). A's page 4 is also sparse, but its layout is more consistent overall.

A has a full-bleed cover with a strong illustration and brown band. Its numbered bold headings are clear, and content flows densely over pages 2-3. The callout sits beside the image, so the text stays legible. B's callout box covers the buildings illustration and looks awkward. B also leaves large empty areas on the cover and on page 3, and its light headings are weaker. B's cover does combine the title and the first section well, and its tables are equivalent to A's. A's heading split across pages (a paragraph breaking from p2 to p3) is a minor flaw.
